name: Reverse engineering

subjectOf.text: Disclosing otherwise private and proprietary Form PF systemic risk data exclusively to bankruptcy judges could alleviate the hedge fund industry's concerns about privacy and about the reverse engineering of its strategies and positions.
subjectOf.abstract: Exclusive disclosure of otherwise private and proprietary systemic risk data in Form PF to bankruptcy judges could potentially alleviate the hedge fund industry's concerns over privacy and reverse engineering of strategies and positions.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463
scope_conditions: judge-only access, with no disclosure to debtors or other creditors

subjectOf.text: The private fund industry's central fear about Form PF was not the filing itself but eventual publicity: if the disclosures ever became public, competitors could reverse engineer fund strategies and largely eliminate managers' ability to generate absolute returns.
subjectOf.abstract: the industry feared that such information could at some point in the future be made public which would largely eliminate private investment fund managers' ability to make absolute returns for their clients as competitors would be able to reverse engineer their strategies. Apart
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016 (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998097
scope_conditions: Form PF disclosures held confidentially by the SEC
